Summarise bowling for one season and phase of the innings

summarise_bowling.Rd

Combines the chosen phases of the innings for each bowler in a season, keeps bowlers who have bowled enough overs, and calculates their economy rate (runs conceded per over). Bowlers are sorted from the lowest economy rate to the highest.

Usage

summarise_bowling(data = wpl_bowling, season_value, phases, min_overs = 2)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing bowling statistics. Defaults to wpl_bowling.

season_value

A single season label, for example "2022/23". Use unique(data$season) to see the options.

phases

One or more phases of the innings, taken from levels(data$phase).

min_overs

Minimum overs a bowler must have bowled in the chosen phases to be included. Defaults to 2.

Value

A data frame with one row per bowler and team, with columns bowler, bowling_team, balls, runs_conceded, wickets and economy. It has zero rows if no bowler bowled enough overs.

Examples

first_season <- sort(unique(wpl_bowling$season))[1]

# Who was cheapest in the powerplay?
summarise_bowling(
  season_value = first_season,
  phases = "Powerplay (overs 1-6)"
)
#> # A tibble: 30 × 6
#>    bowler          bowling_team              balls runs_conceded wickets economy

#>  4 NR Sciver-Brunt Mumbai Indians              114           107       3    5.63

#>  6 IECM Wong       Mumbai Indians               96           100       6    6.25
#>  7 HK Matthews     Mumbai Indians               54            58       6    6.44

# Raise the minimum to compare only the bowlers who bowled the most
summarise_bowling(
  season_value = first_season,
  phases = "Death (overs 16-20)",
  min_overs = 4
)
